title: Lexeme prefetch crediting timeline and cache-impact insights
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We currently surface request-level latency and coarse cache hit rates, but teams struggle to understand how prefetching and KV cache mechanics change per-lexeme costs over the life of a request. This ticket scopes instrumentation and a lightweight aggregation pipeline to produce a lexeme-level timeline (chronology of generation steps) that attributes timing and inferred cost delta to cache events (hit/miss/prefetch). Goals: 1) record a compact lexeme timeline per request capturing emission timestamp, model step, cache decision (hit/miss/prefetch), and upstream routing variant; 2) compute aggregation views that show average latency delta and token-cost delta for cache-prefetch vs on-demand fetch across models and sequence-length cohorts; 3) provide panels and alerting for regressions and cost anomalies; 4) ensure data cost and retention are bounded with sampling and summarization rules. Why now: teams are enabling more aggressive prefetch and LRU heuristics; we need to quantify unit economics and avoid regressions that inflate CPU/GPU cost or increase  tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: every inference request emits a compact lexeme_timeline event with fields: request_id, timestamp_ms, lexeme_index, lexeme_text_hash, model_variant, step_type (emit|prefetch|kv_hit|kv_miss), latency_ms

Pipeline: events are ingested into the metrics pipeline (Clickhouse/OLAP) with a rollup job that computes per-model and per-variant summaries (p95 latency delta by cache status, avg token-cost delta) on a daily cadence
Dashboards: Grafana panels exist showing timeline heatmaps, cache-prefetch effectiveness, and a comparison widget between prefetch-enabled and baseline routing
Alerts: anomaly alert when per-lexeme avg cost increases > 25% week-over-week for any model variant
Sampling & Retention: end-to-end sampling reduces event volume by >= 80% while preserving cohort fidelity; raw events retained for 7 days, rollups for 90 days
implementation_notes: Add lexeme_timeline hook in serving runtime right after emission and after KV cache lookup; keep payload under 200 bytes per event by hashing lexeme text and using enumerated enums for step_type
Use current event bus (kafka/ingest) with a separate topic 'telemetry.lexeme_timeline' to enable independent retention and throughput controls
Pipeline: Chi consumer writes raw events to a compact table with partitioning by model_variant/date; daily rollup job computes aggregates and materializes summary tables used by Grafana
Sampling: apply stratified sampling at the edge with high-fidelity capture for 1% of requests, and deterministic cohort-based sampling for experiments/chosen customers
Privacy: do not store raw lexeme text; only keep lexeme_text_hash and coarse length bucket
Backfill: provide a short backfill script to recompute rollups for last 14 days if we tweak schema
Performance: instrumentation path must add <150us p99 overhead on hot path; measure and gate with microbenchmarks
telemetry_events: lexeme_timeline: {request_id, ts_ms, lexeme_index, lexeme_text_hash, lexeme_len_bucket, model_variant, step_type, latency_ms, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, routing_bucket}
lexeme_prefetch_summary: {model_variant, date, prefetched_tokens, used_prefetch_ratio, avg_latency_delta_ms, token_cost_delta}
kv_cache_effects_rollup: {model_variant, seq_len_bucket, kv_hit_rate, p50_latency_hit, p95_latency_miss, inferred_token_cost_hit, inferred_token_cost_miss}
